title: Rate limit configuration doubles as the venue whitelist, so permission and sizing are the same control
content:
The phrase "The rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for vaults" appears verbatim for `depositERC4626` (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.3.1.1), `requestDepositERC7540` (…2.4.1.1) and `requestRedeemERC7540` (…2.4.2.1), and in swap form as "the rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for swaps" for the PSM functions.

One mechanism therefore answers two questions that are usually separated. *May we interact with this venue?* and *how much may we move?* collapse into a single keyed value: an unset or zero limit makes the call revert, so absence of permission is expressed as absence of capacity.

The elegance is that it removes a class of bug. There is no way for a venue to be whitelisted but unlimited, or limited but unauthorised, because the two states cannot diverge — a common failure in systems that maintain an allowlist and a limits table separately.

It also relocates onboarding authority. Because rate limit data can only be written by `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.2.1.3.2), and that role is held by Sky Governance, **adding a new venue to Obex's Liquidity Layer is a Sky Governance action**, not an Obex one. The Relayer chooses among permitted venues; Sky decides what the permitted set is.

The trade-off is expressiveness: a venue Sky wants to permit for a trivial test amount is indistinguishable in kind from one it endorses at scale — the only difference is a number.
description: A vault or swap route with no configured rate limit simply cannot be used — there is no separate allowlist, and adding a venue means an admin-only rate limit write.
